headline: 84 detained as DB uncovers drug den at DIG's house in Dhaka
summary: Additional DIG Abdullah Al Zahir has been closed following a raid on a property he rented out online, where a large quantity of drugs were recovered.
details: The Detective Branch (DB) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) conducted a raid on a house in the Vatara area of the capital, which was rented out by Additional DIG Abdullah Al Zahir.
During the operation, which lasted from Monday night until Tuesday afternoon, police recovered a large quantity of drugs and detained 84 people.
Among those detained, 26 are women. Police reported that people of various ages, both men and women, visited the house to consume drugs.
Following the incident, the Inspector General of Police (IGP) Mo. Ali Hossain Fakir signed an office order to close Additional DIG Abdullah Al Zahir.
The officer, who was working in the Repair and Maintenance branch of the Police Headquarters, has been attached to the Police Headquarters effective immediately.
caption:
A senior police officer's rented house was turned into a drug den. 84 people were detained in a massive raid.

The Detective Branch (DB) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) conducted a raid on a house in the Vatara area of the capital, which was rented out by Additional DIG Abdullah Al Zahir.

During the operation, which lasted from Monday night until Tuesday afternoon, police recovered a large quantity of drugs and detained 84 people.

Among those detained, 26 are women. Police reported that people of various ages, both men and women, visited the house to consume drugs.

Following the incident, the Inspector General of Police (IGP) Mo. Ali Hossain Fakir signed an office order to close Additional DIG Abdullah Al Zahir.

The officer, who was working in the Repair and Maintenance branch of the Police Headquarters, has been attached to the Police Headquarters effective immediately.

headline_marked: Tarique Rahman [[first PM to visit JM Sen Hall]] during Durga Puja
headline: Tarique Rahman first PM to visit JM Sen Hall during Durga Puja
summary: The Prime Minister visited the historic Chattogram venue on Maha Nabami, marking the first time a head of government has attended celebrations there.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman visited the JM Sen Hall pandal in Chattogram on Tuesday evening during the Maha Nabami celebrations of Durga Puja.
Organisers of the event hailed the visit as a historic milestone, stating that he is the first prime minister to ever attend the festival celebrations at this specific venue.
The Prime Minister was welcomed by leaders of the Bangladesh Puja Udjapan Parishad and the Hindu Religious Welfare Trust, amid excitement from crowds lining the roads.
JM Sen Hall, located in Rahmatganj, has been a principal centre for Durga Puja in Chattogram for over 40 years and is historically linked to anti-British movements.
As part of a wider tour, Tarique Rahman also visited Puja pandals in Rangpur and Rajshahi earlier on Tuesday before arriving in Chattogram.
The visit concluded with a scheduled stop at the Chattogram Circuit House before his return flight to Dhaka.
caption:
A historic first for Chattogram's JM Sen Hall: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman becomes the first PM to visit the venue during Durga Puja.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman visited the JM Sen Hall pandal in Chattogram on Tuesday evening during the Maha Nabami celebrations of Durga Puja.

Organisers of the event hailed the visit as a historic milestone, stating that he is the first prime minister to ever attend the festival celebrations at this specific venue.

The Prime Minister was welcomed by leaders of the Bangladesh Puja Udjapan Parishad and the Hindu Religious Welfare Trust, amid excitement from crowds lining the roads.

JM Sen Hall, located in Rahmatganj, has been a principal centre for Durga Puja in Chattogram for over 40 years and is historically linked to anti-British movements.

As part of a wider tour, Tarique Rahman also visited Puja pandals in Rangpur and Rajshahi earlier on Tuesday before arriving in Chattogram.

The visit concluded with a scheduled stop at the Chattogram Circuit House before his return flight to Dhaka.
